title: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah
hookLine: almost all that is left of her is a name the poor gave her, and she died soon after the marriage

cards: Some people leave diaries. Some leave buildings. Some leave a single name, and the name says a great deal.

Of today's mother of the believers, the sources keep very little: no long speeches, no well-known scenes. The early biographers say she married the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and died not long after.
And they say what people called her: umm al-masakin. The mother of the poor. Today: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah.

teach.b: It's worth being honest at the start. The hadith collections this path usually draws on say little about Zaynab bint Khuzaymah.
What we have comes mostly from the biographers, Ibn Sa'd among them, and it is short: her marriage, her early death, and her name. But consider what a title like that suggests.
Nobody is called the mother of the poor for one good afternoon.

teach.h: A NAME EARNED MEAL BY MEAL.
teach.b: Some readers hear in it the people at her door, the ones who kept coming back because someone kept feeding them: a reputation built meal by meal. And the name sits right inside what the Qur'an praises.

teach.h: WE FEED YOU FOR ALLAH ALONE.
teach.b: In surah seventy-six, the righteous are described as feeding the needy, the orphan and the captive, for love of Allah, and saying, in effect: we feed you for Allah's sake alone; we want no reward from you and no thanks.

teach.h: LIKE ONE WHO PRAYS ALL NIGHT.
teach.b: In Bukhari, the Prophet says that the one who looks after the widow and the poor is like one who strives in the way of Allah, or like one who prays all night and fasts all day.
So the mother of the poor was doing the kind of work the Prophet set alongside prayer and fasting. There's a quiet lesson in how little we know.
Zaynab's life comes down to us almost entirely as what she did for people who couldn't repay her. If only one line of your story survived, it could do worse than that.

how: Muslims remember Zaynab bint Khuzaymah among the mothers of the believers by her title umm al-masakin, and feeding the poor is a regular act of charity on this path, often given in someone's memory.

games.q: you feed someone hungry, and they start to thank you at length. in surah 76, what do the righteous say?
o: we feed you for Allah's sake; we want no reward or thanks.
pass it on to someone else.
games.why: surah 76 has them feed the needy, the orphan and the captive, wanting no reward from them and no thanks.

practice: Bring to mind the last meal you ate, and taste it again for a moment. Then think of someone near you, in your town or on your street, who may not have had one today, and picture a meal reaching them, with no thanks expected.
If you pray, remember Zaynab by name.

wordCard.voice: Zaynab, bint Khuzaymah, called umm al-masakin, the mother of the poor, the title that survives of her, earned by feeding those who couldn't repay her. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'mother of the poor', her title.

carryVoice: Your line: mother of the poor. A whole life, kept in one name. Day eight hundred thirteen, and counting.
